summary: The neighborhood's planned central park of about 1.1 acres in the Port's January 2018 memo (the March 2012 proposal's parcel table gives 1.32 acres, 57,626 sq ft, while its block plan labels the square 0.7 acres), an urban green framed by Blocks E and F with a lawn, a plaza with an interactive spray ground, a cafe pavilion and a tree bosque with retail kiosks; the Design Controls require wind protection, public restrooms and preserved water views. The Draft EIR includes a 700-space garage beneath it. No source read reports it built or assigns it to a phase; the Port's June 2026 Phase 2 report does not mention the square, and the Commission approved up to $10 million of Phase 2 pre-development funding on June 9, 2026 (minutes).

milestones.text: Port Commission approves the Mission Rock Disposition and Development Agreement (Resolution No. 18-03) and consents to the Special Use District zoning and approves the Design Controls (Resolution No. 18-04) that set this block's use and envelope (among Resolutions 18-03 to 18-10, which the Jan 30, 2018 minutes record as adopted; Item 11A, minutes pp.4-5 and 19)

The Notice of Determination gives March 6, 2018 as the date the City 'decided to carry out or approve the project' and lists the Board of Supervisors' final actions, including File No. 171286 (affirming the Planning Department's certification of the Final EIR) and File No. 180092 (the DDA); it was filed March 9, 2018. The Board's own records date two of the other approvals earlier: Resolution 42-18 (the DDA, File 180092) was adopted February 13, 2018, and Ordinance 33-18 (the Development Agreement, File 171313) was finally passed February 27, 2018. The Port's Oct 2023 report calls No. 33-18 a Resolution and its June 2026 report an Ordinance; the Board's file shows an ordinance

Development Agreement takes effect (the Port's fact sheet lists the DA effective date as Aug. 15, 2018, with a 30-year term and 4 phases); the Planning page dates both the Development Agreement and the DDA 8/15/2018
Draft EIR describes a 227,200 gsf below-grade garage of up to 700 spaces under the square as part of the project and places the square and garage in illustrative construction Area 3 (2019-2022)
Developer sends the Port its Phase 2 Submittal (with a Garage Report submitted October 14, 2022 and a Basis of Design November 18, 2022); the budget and appraisal elements are deferred

Port Commission adopts Resolution 23-46 (passed unanimously as amended, with non-substantive changes); its recitals state that Phase 2 is 'not currently financially feasible' and that Port and Developer staff 'mutually agreed earlier this year to decelerate work on Phase 2 while waiting for macroeconomic conditions to improve'

Port staff say later phases 'may require higher percentages of BMR units' to reach the project's 40% target after Phase 1 was cut to 132 BMR units; the Port, developer and MOHCD are reviewing changes 'with the goal of improving the feasibility of future Phases of Mission Rock and accelerating development' (Resolution 25-17)

details.text: Use of Mission Rock Square: the March 2012 Revised Proposal (the developer's proposal, not an adopted plan) describes an urban neighborhood park with multi-use lawn, plaza with interactive spray ground, cafe pavilion, bosque with retail kiosks and an arts program site. The adopted Design Controls (Sec. 3.3) call for a civic 'living room' square with a large flexible open area for temporary uses and events, wind protection through tree planting, one permanent retail and food structure with public restrooms, at least one stormwater treatment garden, and views to the Bay maintained.

open_questions: Which phase will deliver the square and whether the below-grade garage option survives: not stated in any Port memo read; the Phase 2 Garage Report was not located.

Cost of the square: none published. Phase 1's China Basin Park inland budget line (Port October 2023 memo, Table 1, 'Inland CBP': $39,184,050 to $40,657,253 revised estimates) is the only comparable figure in the Port memos.

The 1.1-acre figure in the 2018 approvals memo, the 1.32 acres in the March 2012 proposal's parcel table and the 0.7 acres its block plan prints beside the square are all unexplained; the traced shape on this record's map is about 1.57 acres after clipping, per its own accuracy note.
Which blocks the December 2022 Phase 2 Submittal covers is not stated in the Port memos read; only the Phase 2 parking garage is named.

No expected-completion date could be sourced for Mission Rock Square. No document read assigns the square to a phase. The Mission Rock Design Controls (208 pages, checked in full) contain no phasing schedule at all, and the Port's October 2023 memo lists the Phase 1 vertical buildings as Parcels A, B, F and G, so neighboring Block F was built in Phase 1 while no source read says whether the square's own construction was part of it. The DDA text itself (Board File 180092, adopted by the Board of Supervisors as Resolution 42-18 on February 13, 2018) was not read, so its Land Use Table and Schedule of Performance target dates are not cited here. Phase 2 was found 'not currently financially feasible' in October 2023, per this record's own milestones. No later Port memo or news source gives a revised target year for the square or for the Project's full buildout, so no basis (record, phase or project) supports an expected-completion date.

Area of Mission Rock Square: the March 2012 Revised Proposal's parcel summary gives 57,626 sq ft / 1.32 acres, and the same proposal's block plan labels the square 0.7 acres; the Port's January 2018 approvals memo describes it as 1.1 acres.
